fields.name: product
fields.title: Product
fields.description: What Tally does, what it is made of and the words that the docs use.

blocks.body: This page defines the words that the {{$d_overview|Tally docs}} use.

blocks.name: $t_event
blocks.body: One error report as the app sent it: the error message, the stack trace, the app version and the device details. It can hold personal data, such as a user ID or an email address.

blocks.name: $t_issue
blocks.body: A group of raw error events that share one cause. Tally keeps an issue after it deletes the raw error events in it.

blocks.name: $t_ret
blocks.body: The time that Tally keeps a raw error event after the event arrives. When the time ends, the purge job deletes the event.
Tally is a small service that collects error reports from apps. This page says what Tally does, what it is made of and what it does not do.

An app sends a report to Tally when an error occurs. Tally stores each report as a {{$t_event|raw error event}}. It groups the events that share one cause into an {{$t_issue|issue}}. A team reads the issues to find and fix the errors in its app.
The {{$d_dec|decisions}} and the {{$d_store|storage requirements}} set how long Tally keeps the events. The {{$d_purge|purge job runbook}} says how the team deletes them.

- Show a team each new error within one minute.
- Keep the stored data small and easy to delete.
- Store only the data that a team needs to fix an error.

- Tally does not monitor the speed or the uptime of an app.
- Tally is not a long-term record of errors. A team that needs one exports its issues.

blocks.name: $m_store
blocks.body: The database that holds the raw error events and the issues. The {{$t_ret|retention period}} sets how much it holds.

blocks.name: $m_purge
blocks.body: A nightly job that deletes each raw error event whose {{$t_ret|retention period}} has ended. The {{$d_purge|purge job runbook}} says how to run it.

fields.name: design
fields.title: Design
fields.description: The decisions and the requirements that set how Tally stores raw error events.

blocks.body: This page records the decisions about Tally. Nobody edits a decision after the team accepts it. A new decision replaces it instead.

decision.title: Keep raw error events for 30 days
decision.statement: Tally keeps each raw error event for 30 days after it arrives. Then the purge job deletes it. Issues stay after their events go.
decision.why: Most teams release once a month. With 30 days, a team can see when an error started in the current release. The storage cost stays known.
options: Keep raw error events for 7 days
Keep raw error events for 30 days
Keep raw error events for 90 days
decision.body:
Rejected:
- 7 days. A team that releases once a month loses the events from the start of the release.
- 90 days. It triples the storage cost, and it keeps personal data longer than a team needs it.

blocks.body: This page states what the {{$m_store|event store}} must do. Each requirement names the decision that it follows.

blocks.name: $r_size
blocks.body: The event store must hold every raw error event for the retention period that {{$D30|the retention decision}} sets, with 20% free space above that amount.

fields.name: operations
fields.title: Operations
fields.description: Guides for the people who run Tally from day to day.

blocks.body: The {{$m_purge|purge job}} deletes raw error events when their retention period ends. This guide says how the job runs and what to do when it fails.

fields.name: Nightly purge
steps: The purge job starts every night at 02:00 UTC.
It deletes each raw error event that arrived more than 30 days ago, as {{$D30|the retention decision}} sets.
It keeps every issue, also when it deletes all the events in that issue.

blocks.body:
1. Open the job log and find the first error.
2. Fix the cause, for example a full disk or a lost database connection.
3. Run the job again with `tally purge --now`.
4. Check that no raw error event is older than the retention period.

first_session.ask: Change Tally's retention period from 30 days to 7 days, to lower the storage cost and the privacy risk.
first_session.confirm_reason: These blocks state no retention period, so they still hold with 7 days.

decision.title: Keep raw error events for 7 days
decision.statement: Tally keeps each raw error event for 7 days after it arrives. Then the purge job deletes it. Issues stay after their events go.
decision.why: Most teams act on an error within a week. A shorter period cuts the storage cost and the privacy risk of personal data in events.
options: Keep raw error events for 7 days
Keep raw error events for 30 days
Keep raw error events for 90 days
decision.recommend_reason: The person asked for 7 days to lower the storage cost and the privacy risk.
decision.body:
Rejected:
- 30 days. It keeps personal data three weeks longer than most teams need it.
- 90 days. It costs the most and keeps personal data the longest.

steps: The purge job starts every night at 02:00 UTC.
It deletes each raw error event that arrived more than 7 days ago, as {{$D7|the retention decision}} sets.
It keeps every issue, also when it deletes all the events in that issue.

ops.body: The event store must hold every raw error event for the retention period that {{$D7|the retention decision}} sets, with 20% free space above that amount.

proposal.title: Keep raw error events for 7 days
proposal.summary: A new decision replaces the 30-day decision. The purge job runbook now says 7 days. The storage requirement keeps its words and now cites the new decision.
